title: Platform Invoke (P/Invoke) awareness without becoming a C++ shop
hook: Platform Invoke (P/Invoke) calls native functions in operating system or third-party dynamic-link libraries (DLLs) from C#. Modern LibraryImport source generation replaces much hand-written DllImport marshalling — you still need to respect calling conventions, string encoding, and resource lifetime.

blocks.text: DllImport and LibraryImport declare extern methods implemented in native code. The runtime marshals parameters — strings as UTF-8 or UTF-16, arrays as pointers — and translates calling conventions. SkiaSharp, SQLite, and GPU libraries wrap P/Invoke in managed APIs. You consume those wrappers; you rarely write raw declarations except for OS utilities or legacy SDKs.

blocks.text: Every P/Invoke boundary is a bug surface: wrong charset corrupts strings, wrong lifetime leaks native handles, wrong thread model crashes SkiaSharp. IDisposable on managed wrappers exists because native resources are outside the garbage collector. Interview answer: know the boundary exists, use official wrappers, and read lifetime docs — not every team needs custom C++.

blocks.title: Boundary discipline
blocks.body: Treat native handles like database connections — short lifetime, explicit release, no finalizer reliance.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Wrong CharSet garbling strings. Holding native pointer after managed array is unpinned. SkiaSharp objects without using — native memory leak until GC finalizer.

interviewTakeaways: P/Invoke is the managed-to-native boundary — marshalling and lifetime matter.
Prefer LibraryImport and official NuGet wrappers over raw declarations.
Native resources need Dispose; GC does not track unmanaged heap.
commonPitfalls: Custom P/Invoke when a maintained wrapper exists.
